newsitem.title: USA: Are ghost inspectors next, U.S. lawyer asks.
newsitem.headline: Are ghost inspectors next, U.S. lawyer asks.

text.p: The thought that homeowners may have to have their houses inspected for ghosts before they can sell them is no laughing matter, a University of Florida law professor said Wednesday.

"It's so easy to laugh at it, but if you're a party to a transaction, it's not necessarily funny," Julian Juergensmeyer, a professor at the University of Florida College of Law, said in a statement issued by the college on the eve of Halloween.

"You thought you had your house sold and you already bought another house. And all of a sudden you discover your buyer can back out because you didn't tell them about something that you didn't think was real," said Juergensmeyer, who has taught on the subject.
There's no known proposal that ghost inspections should be added to the list of requirements for home-sellers.

But Juergensmeyer cited the case of a New York City man who bought a house in Nyack, north of the city, and was horrified to learn it was known as the dwelling of poltergeists, which allegedly had been seen by the seller and her family many times over the previous nine years.
The man went to court to overturn the sale -- and won, Juergensmeyer said.
The outcome frightened him, he said, because it left home owners with a problem that might only be possible to fix by calling in an exorcist.
